TDWG maintains information about the standard DwC terms in a few different places:

- The [Darwin Core Quick Reference Guide](https://dwc.tdwg.org/terms/) website.
- Various [term lists](https://github.com/tdwg/dwc/tree/master/dist) on the TDWG DwC Github, including:
  - ac.tdwg.org - Audiovisual Core
  - chrono.tdwg.org
  - chrono iri
  - dublin core dc and dublin core terms (https://www.dublincore.org/specifications/dublin-core/dcmi-terms/)
  - dwc.tdwg.org
  - dwciri
  - Humboldt Core eco.tdwg.org
  - Humboldt IRI
- The DwC [term versions](https://github.com/tdwg/dwc/blob/master/vocabulary/term_versions.csv) CSV, with information about each term's release, version update, and/or deprecation date, among other information.

For IRI lists, found the following quote that sheds some light [here](https://www.tdwg.org/news/2026/mineralogy-extension-terms-ratified/):

> Darwin Core publishes many of its terms in two namespaces:
>
> - dwc: terms take literal values, that is, text or numbers as they appear in a record, such as dwc:hazardType = “radioactive”.
> - dwciri: terms have the same meaning as their dwc: analogues, but their values must be IRIs. An IRI identifies a resource on the web, such as a concept in a controlled vocabulary. An example is dwciri:hazardType = a link to the “radioactive” concept in a published hazard vocabulary. These terms make the data machine-actionable as Linked Data. The Darwin Core RDF Guide explains how to use them.

## Save DwC Quick Reference Guide to CSV

We will first run a script pull most of the information from the Quick Reference Guide (QRG) site (omitting the term examples text) into a local CSV, saved to `../data/external/tdwg/dwc_quick_reference_terms.csv`, and also load it into a `tdwg_terms` dataframe. The QRG site usually lists a class / term collection name prior to listing the terms that are part of this class/collection. The script only creates new rows for terms, but adds the term's class membership as a separate column. For more details see the comments in the script header.

Note that the script will overwrite the existing CSV by default. It may be worth checking the TDWG GitHub term_versions.csv file prior to running this script to see if new terms have been released since it was last run.

```{r}
source("../scripts/data_processing/parse_tdwg_dwc_terms.R")
tdwg_terms <- parse_tdwg_dwc_terms()
head(tdwg_terms)
nrow(tdwg_terms)
```

A few notes about the DwC QRG page:

- Two sections, as listed, aren't technically classes. "Record-level" (8 terms) and "UseWithIRI" (119 terms) are page sections, not classes, so their terms get the section name in the class column. UseWithIRI holds the IRI versions of terms from many different classes.
- Class assignment follows the page layout. For example, ecoiri:absentTaxa sits under MachineObservation on the page, so that's the class it is assigned.
- Classes with no terms don't appear. Classes like LivingSpecimen and PreservedSpecimen have no terms of their own, so they aren't in the CSV.
